title: Noise stability and the lower-left probability
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function whose mean under the uniform distribution on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is zero. Form a random pair $(X,Y)$ by choosing $X$ uniformly and, independently in each coordinate, setting $Y_i=X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and $Y_i=-X_i$ otherwise. Then the noise stability satisfies $\mathbb{E}[f(X)f(Y)]=4\,\mathbb{P}(f(X)=-1\text{ and }f(Y)=-1)-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f$ has mean zero under the uniform distribution
